title: Prefiltered tenant turnstile + contextual anomaly streaming for usage/cost/latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Console receives high-cardinality telemetry (per-tenant usage, cost, latency) and our existing batch detectors produce many false positives for noisy tenants and short-lived spikes. This ticket implements an ingestion-side prefilter and a tenant-turnstile that gates and enriches events into a contextual streaming anomaly pipeline. Goals: reduce false positives, surface correlated multi-signal anomalies (cost+latency+errors), and enable per-tenant adaptive sensitivity while keeping end-to-end detection latency under 90s for critical signals.
acceptance_criteria: Prefilter runs at ingestion and drops >50% low-signal noise for high-throughput tenants without losing >2% of labeled anomalies (based on historical eval set)
Per-tenant adaptive thresholding reduces alert volume for top-10 noisy tenants by >=65% while maintaining global recall >=90% on evaluation prompts
End-to-end anomaly-to-alert latency median < 60s and 95th percentile < 120s for intraday signals
New alerts include contextual enrichment: tenant plan, recent deployment IDs, correlated metric list, and top-3 likely root causes
False positive rate on evaluation holdout < 8% and business-impacting alerts suppressed by auto-mute rules within 10m
Docs, dashboards and runbook updated: design doc in Confluence, dashboard in Looker, runbook in PagerDuty playbook
implementation_notes: Architecture: add a prefilter step (Kafka topic telem-prefilter) upstream of detectors. Prefilter will apply lightweight heuristics + sampling + tenant turnstile counters to avoid over-alerting from noisy tenants.
Enrichment: join incoming events with tenant metadata (plan, SLO tier, known spike windows) from tenant-service cache; attach last-5min baseline summaries computed by aggregation service.
Detection: modify streaming detector to accept contextual fields and run cohort-relative z-scoring; keep global detector fallback for low-cardinality signals.

Turnstile behavior: per-tenant sliding window token bucket with configurable elasticity. Tokens are replenished by background policy; turnstile resets on deployment events to allow new spikes through for initial monitoring.
Suppression/Auto-mute: implement policy engine that mutes alerts for tenants meeting sustained high-noise heuristics and surfaces a warning instead of a page.
Infra: new topics telem-prefilter and telem-enriched in Kafka, consumer group anomaly-streamers-v2; ensure topic retention and partitioning by tenant_id for ordered handling.
Privacy/Security: tenant metadata join runs in VPC; no PII surfaced in alerts. KMS used for any secrets. Security review required before release.
test_plan: Unit tests for prefilter heuristics and turnstile counters (edge cases: bursty arrivals, clock skew)
Integration test standing up telem-prefilter topic with synthetic tenants mimicking top-100 noisy patterns
Golden dataset A/B evaluation comparing current detector vs new pipeline on 90-day history to measure FP/FN and time-to-detect
Chaos test: simulate broker lag and ensure graceful backpressure and alert degradation (no spurious pages)
Canary: rollout pipeline for 5% of tenants (non-enterprise) for 72h, monitor alert rate, CPU, and consumer lag metrics

rollout_plan: Phase 0 - internal validation: run pipeline against historical replay in staging (2 weeks)
Phase 1 - canary: route 5% of production tenants for 72h, monitor FP/FN, consumer lag, and CPU (Canary window: 2025-03-15 to 2025-03-18)
Phase 2 - progressive rollout: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 2 weeks with rollback policy if alert volume drops unexpectedly or false negatives increase beyond threshold
Phase 3 - enable adaptive mute rules for noisy tenants and flag in-console banner for affected customers
monitoring_and_alerting: New metrics: prefilter_drop_rate, turnstile_throttle_rate_by_tenant, enrichment_cache_miss, anomaly_pipeline_e2e_latency_ms
Dashboards: prefilter health, per-tenant alert delta, canary comparison panel
SLOs: e2e detection latency p50 < 60s, p95 < 120s. Alert precision baseline must not degrade by more than 5% vs current.
Alerts: high consumer lag (>30s), turnstile token exhaustion rate surge, enrichment cache failure rate >1%
decisions: Keep prefilter stateless and deterministic (no ML at ingestion) to reduce operational complexity and make backfills reproducible
Use tenant turnstile token bucket with tenant-configurable elasticity; privilege SLO-tier tenants with higher token budgets
Enrichment happens in-stream but reads tenant metadata from read-replicas with local caching to avoid blocking the Kafka consumer
Implement cohort-relative scoring downstream rather than per-tenant absolute thresholds to balance sensitivity across customer segments
